problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-6 & -8 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the second column of the matrix $P?$

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,z=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
First, notice that the Jordan matrix $J$ consists of one Jordan block $J={J}_{2}(-2).$  

Therefore, the columns of $P$ form the following chain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{2}(-2) & : & {v}_{2}\overset{A-(-2)I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A-(-2)I\,}{\to }0 & \end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the second column of $P$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $2$ corresponding to $\lambda =-2.$ 

Now, computing $A-(-2)I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-(-2)I & =[\begin{aligned}-6 & -8 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -8 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Among the given vectors, only $x$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $2,$ since

$$
(A-(-2)I)x=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -8 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=y,
$$

and, therefore,

$$
(A-(-2)I)^{2}x=(A+2I)y=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -8 \\ 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],
$$

and we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\overset{A-(-2)I\,}{\to }[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\overset{A-(-2)I\,}{\to }0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The other vectors do not satisfy this condition.
